en.name: Filo pastry
en.summary: Frozen filo keeps 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F), sealed and stored flat. Once the roll is opened, rewrap it tightly and use it within 3–5 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Both figures are read across from puff pastry — no agency publishes a filo timeline.
en.pantry: Filo is not a room-temperature food, and on an open bench it is barely a ten-minute food: the sheets are paper-thin and unprotected by fat, so they dry into brittle shards almost as you watch. Keep the stack you are not working with under a damp tea towel and take one sheet at a time. The sealed product belongs in the freezer or the fridge, never in the cupboard.
en.fridge: 3–5 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below once the roll has been opened, rewrapped tightly in plastic so no air reaches the edges. That figure is our own conservative reading rather than a published one, since no authority gives an opened figure for pastry sheets. Chilled, never-frozen filo from a Turkish or Greek shop is fresh yufka and is a different thing again: it behaves like fresh dough, and you go by its printed date, which is usually a matter of days.
en.freezer: 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F), the roll sealed and frozen flat. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond that window; the limit is quality, as the sheets dry, crack and weld together. Thaw it slowly — overnight in the fridge, then an hour at room temperature still in its wrapper — because thawing it fast, or refreezing a thawed roll, is exactly what makes the sheets crack and stick. Never stand a frozen roll on its end; the sheets crease and tear along the fold.
en.thawing: Overnight in the fridge and then a short rest at room temperature, still wrapped. Do not thaw filo in a microwave or in warm water, and do not refreeze a roll you have already unrolled.
spoilage: Sheets welded together so they tear instead of separating.
Dry, cracked edges or a roll that shatters when unrolled.
Ice crystals inside the wrapper, which means the roll part-thawed and refroze.
A stale or rancid smell, or any mould on a chilled roll past its date.
tips: Freeze and store the roll flat, never standing on end.
Thaw slowly in the fridge; fast thawing is the main cause of welded sheets.
Work with a damp tea towel over the stack and one sheet at a time.
Brush every sheet with butter or oil as you layer — that is what keeps the shards from drying.

faq.q: How long does frozen filo pastry last?
faq.a: 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F), sealed and stored flat. It stays safe longer if it never thaws, but the sheets dry and crack.

faq.q: How long does opened filo keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 3–5 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, rewrapped tightly in plastic. That is a conservative reading rather than a published figure.

faq.q: Why do my filo sheets stick together?
faq.a: Almost always because the roll was thawed too fast, or thawed and refrozen. Thaw it overnight in the fridge and then briefly at room temperature, still wrapped.

zh.name: 薄酥皮
zh.summary: 冷凍薄酥皮密封平放，在 −18 °C 下可放 12 個月。整卷拆封之後請重新包緊，放 4 °C 以下冷藏 3～5 天內用完。這兩個數字都是比照冷凍酥皮讀過來的——沒有機關為薄酥皮公布期限。
zh.pantry: 薄酥皮不是常溫食品，而且攤在檯面上的它連十分鐘都撐不太住：每一張薄如紙、又沒有油脂保護，你幾乎可以看著它乾成脆片。還沒用到的那疊請蓋上擰乾的濕布，一次只抽一張。未拆封的產品該待在冷凍或冷藏，絕對不是櫃子裡。
zh.fridge: 整卷拆封後用保鮮膜緊緊重新包好，放 4 °C 以下 3～5 天。這個數字是我們保守的判斷，不是公布的數據，因為沒有權威機關給過酥皮拆封後的期限。另外，土耳其或希臘店裡那種冷藏、從沒冷凍過的薄皮是新鮮 yufka，又是另一回事：它的行為就像新鮮麵團，請依包裝上的日期，通常只有幾天。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 12 個月，整卷密封、平放冷凍。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全；限制它的是品質：薄皮會變乾、龜裂、黏成一整塊。請慢慢解凍——冷藏隔夜，再連著包裝在室溫放一小時——因為快速解凍，或把解凍過的整卷再冷凍，正是讓薄皮裂開黏死的原因。冷凍時不要把整卷立起來放，折到的地方會壓出摺痕、一攤就破。
zh.thawing: 冷藏隔夜解凍，再連著包裝在室溫放一下。不要用微波或溫水解凍薄酥皮，也不要把已經攤開過的整卷再冷凍。
spoilage: 薄皮黏死在一起，一撕就破而不是一張張分開。
邊緣乾裂，或整卷攤開時直接碎掉。
包裝內有冰晶，表示它曾經半退冰又再凍回去。
聞起來走味或油耗；冷藏的整卷過期後長霉。
tips: 整卷平放冷凍與保存，絕對不要立著放。
在冷藏慢慢解凍；解凍太快是薄皮黏死的主因。
操作時那疊蓋擰乾的濕布，一次只抽一張。
每疊一張就刷一次奶油或油——那才是讓它不會乾成碎片的關鍵。

faq.q: 冷凍薄酥皮可以放多久？
faq.a: −18 °C 下 12 個月，密封平放。只要沒退冰放更久仍然安全，但薄皮會變乾龜裂。

faq.q: 拆封的薄酥皮冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 用保鮮膜包緊、放 4 °C 以下 3～5 天。這是保守的判斷，不是公布的數字。

faq.q: 薄酥皮為什麼會黏成一整塊撕不開？
faq.a: 幾乎都是因為解凍太快，或是解凍後又冷凍過。請冷藏隔夜、再連包裝在室溫放一下慢慢解。
